content_of_post_to_comment:
If someone told me a few years ago that building your own rules means losing half the crowd, I would have panicked.
Today?
That was the goal.
Somewhere along the way, I stopped measuring my life by how many people stayed. I used to think losing people meant something had gone wrong. So I explained more. Compromised more. Stayed a little longer.
Made myself easier to understand, easier to accept, easier to keep around.
Until one day I realised something.
Some people are only comfortable with the version of you that requires the least from them.
Raise your standards and the room gets quieter.
In love.
In friendship.
At work.
Even in families.
At first, that silence can feel like loss.
Then life begins filling it with people, places and opportunities that don’t require you to negotiate yourself down just to belong.
Maybe losing half the crowd was never the price.
Maybe it was the filter. 💫
comment: I think there’s a difference between setting boundaries and simply cutting people off when they disagree with us. The hardest part is learning who is uncomfortable with your growth versus who is just adjusting to a new version of you. Sometimes the quieter room is also where you notice which relationships were built on mutual respect.
